Quick technical notes from my side after looking at the headers you attached:
- The forwarding system is performing SRS (Sender Rewriting Scheme); that rewrites the envelope-from and commonly causes our one-click accept token (embedded as a query parameter on the acceptance URL) to be dropped by intermediary rewriting/proxy behaviors.
- Two mitigation options we can ship quickly:
  1) Issue invites where the token is included both in the URL and as a short one-time code in the email body (users can copy/paste the code on the acceptance page).
  2) Use a POST-based acceptance endpoint where we accept an invite via a short GUID submitted from a small form we host — this is somewhat more resilient to intermediate rewrites because it doesn't rely on envelope-to redirect preservation.

I recommend option (1) as a same-day fix. I will prepare the link template and an alternate acceptance page and post the acceptance endpoint to a short-lived URL: https://app.redwood.ai/invite/alt/7f3b2c

Laura — please confirm we can include the token in the email body for these customers (it's a one-time code, 6 characters).

Ben — can you reissue the three invites and include the code in the email body?

-Karthik
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

Jordan / Marta,

We captured the forwarded message chain and attached the trace; our provider rewrites Return-Path and prepends SRS tags like SRS0=HASH=originaldomain=localpart using our relay. The user pasted the acceptance URL and it shows only the base path: https://portal.anchorlogistics.com/accept (no query string).

Attached: srs_trace.txt (showing Received lines and rewrite examples).

If you can provide a one-time code in the body, users can enter it on the acceptance page. Alternately we can whitelist your sending domain in forwarding for a short window if that helps (requires change ticket, may take 24–48 hrs).
